chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadil, from Abu al-Subah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And when you enter houses, then send peace upon yourselves' — the verse — so he said: It is the man's sending of peace upon the people of the house when he enters, and then they respond to him. That is your sending of peace upon yourselves.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ: People of the house / household members

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'send peace upon yourselves' mean in the context of entering a house?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a contextual interpretation of Quran 24:61, explaining that 'saluting yourselves' refers to the host's greeting upon the guests' entry, with the guests' response fulfilling the command. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the social etiquette of *salam* as a reciprocal act of peace and recognition within the domestic sphere, reinforcing the bond between host and guest.
